description: Keep films whose rental duration is 5 days or more, so films with exactly 5 days count.

d.request: Filter to films with `rental_duration >= 5`, then group by `rating`. For each rating, return the rating, the average of `rental_rate / rental_duration` across films with nonmissing values for that ratio, the total number of films in the group, and that average divided by the unweighted mean of the per-rating averages across all ratings. Return no rows if that benchmark is missing, and leave all values unrounded.
d.sql:
WITH rating_averages AS (
  SELECT
    rating,
    AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day,
    COUNT(*) AS film_count
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration >= 5
    AND rental_rate IS NOT NULL
    AND rental_duration IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY rating
),
benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS mean_rating_average
  FROM rating_averages
)
SELECT
  ra.rating,
  ra.avg_rate_per_day,
  ra.film_count,
  ra.avg_rate_per_day / b.mean_rating_average AS relative_to_mean
FROM rating_averages AS ra
CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b
WHERE b.mean_rating_average IS NOT NULL;

c.request: Treating 5 days as the cutoff for a long rental period, look only at the long-rental films (by `rental_duration`) and group them by `rating`. For each rating, show the rating, the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values), the number of films, and that average divided by an overall benchmark. The benchmark is the plain unweighted mean of the per-rating averages across all ratings, ignoring any missing ones. If the benchmark itself is missing, return no rows. Leave all values unrounded. Keep films whose rental duration is 5 days or more, so films with exactly 5 days count.
c.sql:
WITH per_rating AS (
  SELECT
    rating,
    AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day,
    COUNT(*) AS film_count
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration >= 5
  GROUP BY rating
), benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS benchmark_avg
  FROM per_rating
)
SELECT
  p.rating,
  p.avg_rate_per_day,
  p.film_count,
  p.avg_rate_per_day / b.benchmark_avg AS avg_to_benchmark
FROM per_rating AS p
CROSS JOIN benchmark AS b
WHERE b.benchmark_avg IS NOT NULL;

a.request: Looking only at films whose `rental_duration` is at least 5 days, group them by `rating`. For each rating, show the rating, the average per film of `rental_rate` divided by `rental_duration` (ignoring missing values), the number of films, and that average divided by an overall benchmark. The benchmark is the plain unweighted mean of the per-rating averages across all ratings, ignoring any missing ones. If the benchmark itself is missing, return no rows. Leave all values unrounded.
a.sql:
WITH rating_averages AS (
  SELECT rating, AVG(rental_rate / rental_duration) AS avg_rate_per_day, COUNT(*) AS film_count
  FROM film
  WHERE rental_duration >= 5
  GROUP BY rating
), benchmark AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_rate_per_day) AS overall_benchmark
  FROM rating_averages
)
SELECT ra.rating, ra.avg_rate_per_day, ra.film_count,
       ra.avg_rate_per_day / b.overall_benchmark AS benchmark_ratio
FROM rating_averages ra
CROSS JOIN benchmark b
WHERE b.overall_benchmark IS NOT NULL
